title: Exact restriction, products and normalized gluing support for clopen strict towers
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and R a sheaf of rings on its fixed small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Ordinary restriction along an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] preserves finite limits and colimits, and preserves the actual countable products with their projection maps [def-weil-category-product]. Module sheaves have exact countable products. For a finite disjoint open-and-closed cover [def-weil-closed-immersion], and R whose section rings are commutative, the recorded module-gluing functor [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] admits additive section coordinates, with its actual unit, counit and both triangle equations unchanged. Products of sections are identified by the canonical projection-normalized additive equivalences. For an additive functor preserving countable products, the fixed strict Roos model [def-weil-strict-roos-model] has its generic diagonal comparison preserving the second projection, all evaluations and the negative-inclusion boundary; applying any functor to these equations retains their actual maps. These are the already proved support calculations of the strict-clopen tower theorem. Empty schemes and empty finite families are included.

proof.text: Use the recorded clopen module restriction and its piece adjunction to obtain exactness. Preserve the ordinary restriction, complex and derived functor definitions verbatim. For countable products, apply weakly contractible covering families and the section-surjectivity product argument of the existing exact-products proof, then reflect epimorphisms through additive presheaves. This is the original proved independent-universe argument.

The generic additive Roos comparison supplies the diagonal two-summand formula and becomes an isomorphism when products are preserved. Compute the fixed boundary as the negative first inclusion, and check projection, evaluation and boundary equations in coordinates. Functoriality gives the localized equations. These are the original proved generic calculations.

Preserve countable products under continuous pushforward by the forgetful functor to additive presheaves. Evaluate product cones to obtain the section coordinate equivalences and their projection equations. Reindex the finite family using Shrink I, apply the recorded module-gluing unit and counit and their triangle equations, then descend the counit through the fully faithful reindexing equivalence. Transpose the section coordinates without changing any entry. All proofs are the existing complete support lemmas, renamed privately only for compatibility wrappers.
